listings.name: Teatro San Gallo
listings.content: Half-hour documentary based on the BBC series Francesco's Venice - an 'amazing film that puts the spectacular beauty of this great city in historical context'. Film in English, audioguides in Italian, Russian and Spanish.

listings.name: E Rosa Salva
listings.content: One of the favorites is the mini-chain "E Rosa Salva", with three locations in the center - on C. Fiubera (from Piazza San Marco, take the underpass in the middle of the arcade, cross the bridge and take second right off C. Fabbri), Merceria S. Salvadore (off the campo of the same name), and right on Campo San Zanipolo (to the right of the church looking from the canal); the last one is a gelateria as well. For your €1 you'll get exactly 2 and a half sips at the bottom of a small cup, with rich crema and no bitterness. Assorted house-made sweets are €1.10.

listings.name: Domus Ciliota
listings.content: A 5-10 minute walk from San Marco's Square. The hotel has over fifty clean, basic, air-conditioned rooms all with shower and WC. The 24-hr reception is English speaking. There is an area for leaving baggage after you've checked out. Single rooms are €70-85 and doubles are €100-110 including breakfast.

listings.name: Hotel Ala
listings.content: Eggs and broiled tomatoes with cheese for breakfast. Rooms were a typical size but clean, comfortable and quiet. They have turndown service at night, a pleasant surprise.
listings.address: Campo Santa Maria dei Gigli, San Marco 2494

listings.name: Hotel All'Angelo Venice
listings.content: Run by the same family since 1924 in a 17th-century building close to St Marks Basilica. Comfortable and stylishly decorated rooms with a double somewhere in the region of €150.

listings.name: Hotel Antico Panada
listings.content: Has rooms decorated in an 18th-century Venetian style.

listings.name: Hotel Becher
listings.content: This 18th-century hotel enhanced by the most modern amenities, charming atmosphere and impeccable service. Single rooms from €70, doubles €110 and triples from €170.

listings.name: Hotel Firenze Venice
listings.content: On a side street of Piazza San Marco, and offers bright and comfortable rooms.
listings.price: Rooms start at around €120 a double/twin

listings.name: Hotel Lisbona Venice
listings.content: Just in front of Piazza San Marco, three star rooms decorated in the grand Venetian style. Double rooms are usually around €140.

listings.name: Hotel Montecarlo Venice
listings.content: 3-star superior rooms and services one hundred yards from the entrance to Basilica San Marco.
listings.price: Rooms start at around €130 a double

listings.name: Hotel San Giorgio
listings.content: The hotel is between Campo Sant'Angelo and Campo Manin in an antique Gothic palace bought by Mariano Fortuny.
listings.price: Single rooms from €60, doubles from €90, triples from €120
listings.address: Rio Terà della Mandola, San Marco 3781

listings.name: Hotel San Moise Venice
listings.content: 3-star hotel behind Piazza San Marco and the Basilica.
listings.price: Starting in the region of €120-140 for a double room

listings.name: Pagan Luxury House
listings.content: According to their website, there is a €10 per night discount for booking directly with them.

listings.name: Hotel Flora
listings.content: Garden, free Wi-Fi, homemade buffet breakfast, fitness centre.

listings.name: Novecento Boutique Hotel
listings.content: Has 9 rooms featuring original furniture and tapestries from both the Mediterranean and the Far East.

listings.name: Locanda Orseolo
listings.content: A 3-minute walk from St. Peter's Square, operated by a multi-lingual Venetian family who offer impeccable concierge service. Room rates are generally €150 to €200.

listings.name: Corte 1321
listings.content: Large spacious rooms with double sink bathrooms ensure a comfortable stay. Lovely courtyard for dining is made memorable with local birds strutting and cooing.

listings.name: Hotel Marconi Venice
listings.content: The hotel overlooks the Grand Canal and famous Rialto Bridge. It has been a hotel since the 1930 and has a very interesting art deco style, with rooms going for around €150, or for a little more with a canal view.

listings.name: Hotel al Sole
listings.content: Hotel is in a noble palace built in the beginning of the 15th century, a short distance from Piazzale Roma.

listings.name: Hotel Basilea Venice
listings.content: Across the Grand Canal from Santa Lucia Train Station. Located in a quiet Calle.
listings.price: Double rooms are usually €100-160 depending on season

listings.name: Hotel Doge Venice
listings.content: Three-star accommodation of Venice. It is in the northern part of the city, in front of the train station and presents 10 bedrooms – single, double and twin, some with a shared bathroom - and one apartment.
listings.price: Double rooms start from €57. Family apartment for three people €97
listings.address: Lista Vecchia dei Bari, Santa Croce 1222

listings.name: Hotel Alla Salute
listings.content: A 16th-century palazzo, a stone's throw from Piazza San Marco. It has been the house of the famous poet Ezra Pound. Pretty comfortable and quiet budget hotel. Garden for breakfast.

listings.name: Belle Arti Hotel Venice
listings.content: Elegant three-star hotel. 67 guestrooms divided in double, triple and quadruple with en suite services, bathroom kit and modern services.
listings.price: Double €220. Breakfast included for those who book online

listings.name: Hotel Palazzo Guardi
listings.content: A stone's throw from the Accademia, is this noble Venetian palace, rooms equipped with all comforts.

listings.name: Hotel Cà D'Oro
listings.content: The hotel is in a quiet corner of Cannaregio district, 5 minutes walk from the Rialto Bridge.

listings.name: Lace Museum
listings.content: There is a small lace museum called Museo del Merletto. Opinions on it vary from "not much to see" to "I didn't think I was interested in lace, but I spent 90 minutes in there". A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Trattoria da Romano
listings.content: Famous people, including royalty, visited the place. The walls are covered with their photo's.

listings.name: Old Jewish Cemetery - Lido
listings.content: Over thousand tombstones dating from 1550 to early 18th century. Guided tours on Sat from May to Oct (Italian and English), booking required.
listings.address: Riviera San Nicolò, Isola del Lido

listings.name: Venice Lido Planetarium
listings.content: Optical-mechanical structure, realistic reproduction of the celestial globe.

listings.name: Votive Temple
listings.content: Military memorial dedicated to Italian soldiers of World War I and II.

listings.name: Monastery of San Nicolò al Lido
listings.content: Monastery and church that houses some relics of Saint Nicholas (270–343 AD), patron of sailors. Both the church and monastery dates back to the 16th century.

listings.name: Mekhitarist Monastery
listings.content: Library with historical manuscripts, collection of works, miniatures and documents of the Armenian history, Monastery Church. Tours in Italian, English, and Armenian. On the small island of San Lazzaro degli Armeni.
listings.address: Isola di San Lazzaro degli Armeni

listings.name: Venice International Film Festival
listings.content: Attend the annual film festival, the oldest of its kind. It is organized by La Biennale di Venezia and usually takes place around late August or early September. Make your reservations early as the island is small and hotels fill up. Many celebrities attend this annual event, so have your camera ready.

listings.name: Oasi Dune degli Alberoni
listings.content: Visit the natural oasis in Alberoni, a WWF June 2020 December 2020 protected area of about 1.6 km² at the southern tip of the Lido.

listings.name: Energy Darshan
listings.content: A center for meditation and relaxation.

listings.name: La Grande Cina
listings.content: Chinese cuisine

listings.name: Trattoria Andri
listings.content: Serves local Venetian seafood delicacies such as squid in ink over polenta (not as bad as it sounds), shrimp scampi and octopus, among other more common dishes. Water is served in Murano glass vases. Inside, pictures of celebrities who've eaten here line the walls, such as Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta Jones. Dine on the terrace, nice ambiance. Locals seem to prefer this place.

listings.name: La Cantinita
listings.content: Mexican cuisine

listings.name: Chiosco Chiringuito
listings.content: A Grill

listings.name: B&B Villa Gabriella
listings.content: Villa Gabriella Dimora Storica Liberty is a part of a villa built in 1922. The design was inspired to the Palladio's Rotonda. Located in the Lido Island (Lido di Venezia is Blue Flag for sea water since 2008!), in front of the Adriatic Sea, it's 20 minutes far from S. Mark Sq. Wonderful panoramic seafront terrace. Last complete restoration: 2010!

listings.name: Hotel Villa Albertina
listings.content: An aristocratic building managed in a personalized and familiar way. The hotel is located only 20 minutes from St. Mark Square.

listings.name: Hotel Panorama
listings.content: Hotel Panorama is an affordable and small yet charming hotel situated across the lagoon from Venice. Rooms are a good size with large windows, great views, and attentive service. It is easily reachable on foot from the waterbus, offering beautiful vistas along with the nearby shopping and dining districts of Lido. It also offers a scenic 2nd floor terrace and the first floor dining room also looks out on the lagoon. Excellent choice of breakfast items.

listings.name: Albergo Quattro Fontane
listings.content: Gracious, 4-star country house hotel, 5 minutes walk from the beach and 15 minutes by Vaporetto to St Marks Square. The spacious rooms are all air-conditioned, there's lovely floral gardens and a large outdoor terrace where you can eat in the shade of a huge, ancient plane tree.

listings.name: Hotel Ausonia Hungaria
listings.content: Inaugurated in 1907, this historic 5-star hotel is built in a stunning Nouveau Art style.

listings.name: Hotel Excelsior
listings.content: Luxury resort on the east coast of Lido island.

listings.name: Basilica dei Santa Maria e San Donato
listings.content: Known for its twelfth-century Byzantine mosaic pavement, which is a similar floor to Venice's Basilica di San Marco, and the mosaic dome in the apse of the Virgin Mary. It is said to house the bones of the dragon slain by Saint Donatus. The bell tower, like most bell towers, is separate from the Church.

listings.name: Chiesa di San Pietro Martire
listings.content: Built in the 15th century and then reconstructed some years later after a fire. Inside are some art works, such as two canvasses by Bellini.

listings.name: Palazzo Da Mula
listings.content: The summer residence of the Venetian patricians. The façade features large Gothic windows and Veneto-Byzantine patere and panels from the 12th and 13th centuries. It is one of the few palazzi which escaped the restructuring of the island in the 1800s.

listings.name: Glass Museum
listings.content: Housed in the large Palazzo Giustinian near the island's center. "Museo Vetrario" in Italian, offers a century-by-century tour of Venetian glass-making. Roman glass pieces dating to the 1st to 3rd cent AD. Largest collection of historical glass with pieces dating from the 15th to 20th centuries. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: La Perla Ai Bisatei
listings.content: Not an easy osteria to find but it is truly worth the detour for the kind service and cuisine.

listings.name: B - Alla Vecchia Pescheria
listings.content: Nice and simple restaurant, also with al fresco dining in the small square. Friendly staff. Try the local specialties.

listings.name: Trattoria Busa alla Torre Da Lele
listings.content: A typical trattoria, frequented by both tourists and locals. Excellent food.

listings.name: Osteriva
listings.content: Venetian cuisine with tasting menu. Mid-to-high priced.
listings.address: Riva Longa 49, Murano Venice, Veneto, 30141 Italy

listings.name: Al Soffiador
listings.content: On the hotel premises is a restaurant. There are two buildings connected by a garden terrace. Each room has its own bathroom. 2 rooms are equipped to host disabled guests.

listings.name: Hotel Locanda Conterie
listings.content: All rooms have a private bathroom.

listings.name: Hyatt Centric Murano Venice
listings.content: Mid-to-high priced hotel, although better deals can be found than the hotel's published rate. Rooms have a safe and mini-bar. Two restaurants: a more casual bar/restaurant, and a more formal sit down restaurant. A benefit is that the hotel (as of April 2022) has a complimentary transfer to and from Venice Marco Polo airport on request; whilst waiting for the transfer back the hotel will also store luggage. For travel to and from the main Venetian islands, the "Museo" vaporetto station is just outside the hotel: the passing routes will take travellers directly to all the main tourist sites of Venice including San Marco (do note that it takes c.40 mins for travel time).

listings.name: Murano Palace
listings.content: Very nice place, very clean, friendly owner. Beautiful views from the balcony.

listings.name: Doge's Palace
listings.content: Don't miss the guided tour named Secret Itinerary, which will let you discover the part of the palace where the city's administration worked, as well as Casanova's jail and the wonderful five hundred year old roof structure. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Bell tower of St. Mark
listings.content: The current tower dates from 1912; an exact replica of the previous tower which collapsed in 1902. The top of the tower offers great views of Venice and the lagoon.

listings.name: Clock tower
listings.content: Having been closed for restoration for many years, the restored astronomical clock is now visible. The fascinating tour of the clock mechanism (and rooftop bell) can only be visited on a guided tour, in English: M-W at 10:00 and 11:00, on other days at 14:00 and 15:00, in French M-W at 14:00 and 15:00, advance reservation required online or by phone at +39 041 5209070. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Ponte di Rialto
listings.content: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

listings.name: Saint Mark's Basilica
listings.content: Saint Mark's Basilica is on the Piazza San Marco and is one of the highlights of a visit to Venice. As with most churches in Italy, you must be dressed appropriately to be allowed in; this means no short skirts or bare shoulders. You are not allowed to carry large bags or rucksacks inside, sometimes even small daypacks may need to be deposited. Storage is available just around the corner from the main entrance (free of charge). Filming and photography is forbidden so be prepared in advance. The visit within the basilica lasts ten minutes. Waiting for entry into the basilica can last up to five or so hours and it may be wise to use a ticket service to reserve your visit (reservation costs €3). Once you have a reservation you can take the group entrance on the left, where you hand in the printout of your reservation.
listings.price: Admission to the basilica is free, however, the museum upstairs costs €5 and to view the high altar and treasury costs €2 and €3 respectively

listings.name: Basilica San Giorgio Maggiore
listings.content: Designed by Andrea Palladio and build 1566-1610. Very nice views of Venice from the bell tower.
listings.price: For the bell tower: €6, reduced rate €4 (students and 65+)
listings.image: Basilica di San Giorgio Maggiore a Venezia.jpg

listings.name: S. Salvatore
listings.content: Includes the tomb of Caterina Cornaro, Queen of Cyprus (1454-1510).

listings.name: Correr Museum
listings.content: Interesting collection of globes, starting from the 16th century. There is also an only library hall, an archeological museum of Roman antiques and an important picture gallery. The museum offers a tour of Venetian history. Remarkable painting gallery with masterpieces of the 14th to 16th centuries from Venice, works of the Venetian sculpture Canova, studies on urban development and social life. At the end of your visit, don't miss the museum art cafe, with their tables on the San Marco Square. A MUVE museum.
listings.address: Piazza San Marco, Ala Napoleonica, San Marco 52
listings.image: 8240 - Venezia - San Marco dal Museo Correr - Foto Giovanni Dall'Orto, 12-Aug-2006.jpg

listings.name: Palazzo Grassi
listings.content: Contemporary art museum. Temporary exhibitions from François Pinault's Collection.

listings.name: Palazzo Fortuny
listings.content: Collection of paintings and lamps. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Telecom Italia Future Centre
listings.content: Centre dedicated to telecommunication technology. The building complex includes an adjacent church with important works of art, the Refectory (which is a conference hall today), Renaissance cloisters and a small museum focusing on the evolution of the telephone in the last 100 years.

listings.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
listings.content: A cylindrical tower with a spiralling series of arches, among the most characteristic examples of Venetian architecture at the period of transition from Gothic to Renaissance styles. From the top there are great panoramic views of the city.
listings.address: Corte del Riso o del Bovolo, San Marco 4303

listings.name: Music Museum
listings.content: Beautiful church, collection of musical instruments, Venetian Baroque paintings. Interpreti Veneziani, the creators of the Music Museum, also offer concerts in the nearby San Vidal church.
listings.address: Chiesa di S.Maurizio, Campo di S.Marizio, San Marco 2603

listings.name: Archaeological Museum
listings.content: Collection of ancient Greek and Roman sculptures, Egyptian, Assyrian and Babylonian artefacts.

listings.name: St.Mark's Basilica Museum
listings.content: Visit the famous bronze horses.

listings.name: Marciana National Library
listings.content: Buildings by Sansovino, most important collection of books in Venice.

listings.name: Giorgio Cini Foundation
listings.content: Multi-functional centre in an old Benedictine dormitory, the heart of the Foundation's library complex

listings.name: La Fenice Theatre
listings.content: One of the best opera houses in the world. The theatre is an identical reconstruction (rebuilt in 2003) of the previous theatre building that burned down in 1996. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available at the theatre, various locations around the city, or by phone +39 041 2424. You can visit this historic theatre with an audioguide (good explanations in several languages).
listings.price: Tours: adults €10, students up to 26 and seniors over 65 €7, children up to 6 free. Slightly cheaper if purchased as part of a combined ticket with the Doge's palace. Performances €10-380

listings.name: Ateneo San Basso
listings.content: Classical concerts.

listings.name: Chiesa San Vidal
listings.content: Classical concerts by Interpreti Veneziani. They also run the nearby Music Museum in the nearby San Maurizio church.

listings.name: Scuola Grande di S.Teodoro
listings.content: Opera and concert performances.

listings.name: Bar Ducale
listings.content: A bistro

listings.name: We Love Italy fresh pasta to go - Rialto
Ristorante Al Conte Pescaor
listings.content: Cozy restaurant with a terrace serving fish dishes and sea food pasta

listings.name: Da Cherubino
listings.content: Italian dishes.

listings.name: Osteria Da Carla
listings.content: An Italian restaurant

listings.name: Antico Martini
listings.content: A luxury restaurant, favorite among the famous names of culture and business, the Antico Martini also attracts expert gourmets and famous personalities since the 1800s who come to enjoy unforgettable flavors. Beautiful detail and restaurant decor, romantic atmosphere. The site has been a restaurant since 1720, with the venue being open since 1952.

listings.name: Restaurant La Caravella
listings.content: Historical place near St. Mark's Square, known since the 1960s, it has become a must if you like traditions. Offers some typical dishes and a large selection of wines. From May to September service is in a traditional courtyard.

listings.name: Caffe Quadri
listings.content: Opposite Caffè Florian, with similar prices.

listings.name: Bistrot de Venise
listings.content: Restaurant, cultural and enogastronomical meetings.

listings.name: Devils Forest Pub
listings.content: A traditional English style pub with a very fun atmosphere. It is located near the Rialto Bridge and tucked into a small alley near the Disney Store.
listings.address: Calle dei Stagneri o de la Fava

listings.name: Caffè Florian
listings.content: On the extravagant side there is Caffè Florian, on Piazza San Marco. It claims to be the oldest coffee house still in operation, established in 1720. The interior is about a century newer, and brings an exclusive setting for a cup of coffee, even if sitting outside overlooking the entire piazza and its surroundings may be a better choice on a nice summer day. The café has its own outdoor orchestra playing an assortment of Italian music. Just sitting down at the table costs €6 per seat (for the orchestra it says on the menu) and the rest on the menu is at least twice the price you would have paid at home. Light lunch or dinner 12:00-15:00, 19:30-22:00, afternoon tea 15:09-18:00, great choice of semifreddo (parfaits) (€14), lemon ice cream with soda (€15), great choice of tea and coffee specialities; espresso €6.50. music charge €6.

listings.name: Harry's Bar-Ristorante
listings.content: The Bellini-cocktail was invented here. Ernest Hemingway was one of the most famous guests. Very pricy!

listings.name: Bed and Breakfast Venice Ca' del Pozzo
listings.content: Completely restructured in 2003, in the characteristic Campo San Maurizio.

listings.name: Ai Do Mori
listings.content: As close as it gets to Piazza San Marco, but on the second and third floor, so it still is quiet at nights. Clean and nice rooms, TV, aircon, very friendly staff.

listings.name: Antico Fiore
listings.content: An 18th-century building which has been carefully restored.

listings.name: Astoria
listings.content: 2-star hotel. It has Wi-Fi at a fee and rooms from €70.

listings.name: Ca' Contarini
listings.content: A small, quiet establishment in a five hundred year old building. Both shared and private rooms are available, no curfew-lockouts, including free Wifi, coffee/tea, and light breakfast.
listings.address: Calle dei Orbi (Corte de la Vida), San Marco 3025

listings.name: Ca' Rialto
listings.content: In a building overlooking the Grand Canal and Rialto Bridge.

listings.name: Hotel Serenissima
listings.content: Completely refurbished at the start of 2007 and is a one-minute walk from the Piazza San Marco.

listings.name: Ateneo Hotel Venice
listings.content: 3-star hotel close to Basilica San Marco.
listings.price: Rooms start at around €120 depending on season

listings.name: Alcyone Hotel Venice
listings.content: Its 26 bedrooms are divided in single, double, triple and superior. All with en suite services, shower, telephone, satellite TV and air conditioning.

listings.name: Antica Casa Coppo
listings.content: Classic Venetian styled rooms starting at €100 a night. Near the Rialto Bridge. Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Antico Casin Locanda
listings.content: A refined example of contemporary design, located close to Saint Mark's Square. Doubles from €90.

listings.name: Domus Ciliota
listings.content: A 5-10 minute walk from San Marco's Square. The hotel has over fifty clean, basic, air-conditioned rooms all with shower and WC. The 24-hr reception is English speaking. There is an area for leaving baggage after you've checked out. Single rooms are €70-85 and doubles are €100-110 including breakfast.

listings.name: Hotel Ala
listings.content: Eggs and broiled tomatoes with cheese for breakfast. Rooms were a typical size but clean, comfortable and quiet. They have turndown service at night, a pleasant surprise.
listings.address: Campo Santa Maria dei Gigli, San Marco 2494

listings.name: Hotel All’Angelo Venice
listings.content: Run by the same family since 1924 in a 17th-century building close to St Marks Basilica. Comfortable and stylishly decorated rooms with a double somewhere in the region of €150.

listings.name: Hotel Antico Panada
listings.content: Has rooms decorated in an 18th-century Venetian style.

listings.name: Hotel Becher
listings.content: This 18th-century hotel enhanced by the most modern amenities, charming atmosphere and impeccable service. Single rooms from €70, doubles €110 and triples from €170.

listings.name: Hotel Firenze Venice
listings.content: On a side street of Piazza San Marco, and offers bright and comfortable rooms.
listings.price: Rooms start at around €120 a double/twin

listings.name: Hotel Lisbona Venice
listings.content: Just in front of Piazza San Marco, three star rooms decorated in the grand Venetian style. Double rooms are usually around €140.

listings.name: Hotel Montecarlo Venice
listings.content: 3-star superior rooms and services one hundred yards from the entrance to Basilica San Marco.
listings.price: Rooms start at around €130 a double

listings.name: Hotel San Giorgio
listings.content: The hotel is between Campo Sant'Angelo and Campo Manin in an antique Gothic palace bought by Mariano Fortuny.
listings.price: Single rooms from €60, doubles from €90, triples from €120
listings.address: Rio Terà della Mandola, San Marco 3781

listings.name: Hotel San Moise Venice
listings.content: 3-star hotel behind Piazza San Marco and the Basilica.
listings.price: Starting in the region of €120-140 for a double room

listings.name: Pagan Luxury House
listings.content: According to their website, there is a €10 per night discount for booking directly with them.

listings.name: Novecento Boutique Hotel
listings.content: Has 9 rooms featuring original furniture and tapestries from both the Mediterranean and the Far East.

listings.name: Palazzina Grassi Hotel
listings.content: First Italian hotel designed by Philippe Starck, the only one in Venice. In the centre, near the Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Saint Mark's Square is a short walk away.

listings.name: Duodo Palace Hotel
listings.content: Four-star luxury hotel.

listings.name: Hotel Al Codega
listings.content: In a picturesque little ‘cortile’ (courtyard), which is a short walk from Piazza San Marco.
listings.address: Corte del Forno Vecchio, San Marco 4435

listings.name: Hotel Dei Dragomanni
listings.content: 4-star hotel in an ancient Venetian palazzo.
listings.address: Calle del Dose da Ponte, San Marco 2711

listings.name: Corte di Gabriela
listings.content: Corte di Gabriela is a 4-star boutique hotel in Venice in an elegant nineteenth-century building, overlooking the canals of the San Marco district. It has a few suites, each different from the others.

listings.name: Hotel Bauer Palazzo
listings.content: Historic luxury hotel facing the Grand Canal. Hotel Bauer has been around since 1880.

listings.name: The Gritti Palace
listings.content: Housed in the Palazzo Pisani Gritti, facing the Grand Canal, this hotel was once the private residency of a 16th century dodge. It has been a hotel since 1895

listings.name: Archaeological Museum
listings.content: Collection of Greek and Roman finds, archaeological finds from the estuary from Paleo-Veneto and Etruscan periods.

listings.name: Basilica di Santa Maria Assunta
listings.content: Precious mosaics, dating from Byzantine times, in the oldest cathedral in the lagoon of Venice. Campanile closed for restoration.

listings.name: Chiesa di Santa Fosca
listings.content: Has the form of a Greek cross, which is surrounded by a semi-octagonal porticus.

listings.name: Locanda Cipriani
listings.content: A rustic and romantic 5-room inn that has hosted several famous guests, including Ernest Hemingway, who wrote Across the River and into the Trees here. Rooms have no TVs but instead a small selection of books. Also has a popular restaurant (reservation required).
listings.price: From €140 per person per night; half-board €50 extra

listings.name: Rialto Bridge
listings.content: The bridge has become one of Venice's most recognizable icons and has a history that spans over 800 years. Today's Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591 and was used to replace a wooden bridge that collapsed in 1524.

listings.name: Campo San Polo
listings.content: A large campo (square), one of the most popular Carnival venues and also used for open-air concerts and screenings during the Venice Film Festival.

listings.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
listings.content: A masterpiece of Tintoretto, this guild house is an exquisite example of Mannerist art at its best. In order to allow a comfortable admiration of the detailed ceiling, mirrors are offered to the visitors. Cycles of allegories, life and passion of Christ, scenes from the Old and New Testament.

listings.name: Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista
listings.content: Monumental staircase by Codussi, splendid San Giovanni Salon, Oratory of the Cross with precious reliquiaries.

listings.name: House of Carlo Goldoni
listings.content: Birthplace of Venice's most famous playwright. Museum, library and theater studies center. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Leonardo da Vinci Museum Venice
listings.content: Small museum dedicated to the life and work of Leonardo da Vinci.

listings.name: San Giacomo di Rialto
listings.content: This church is possibly the oldest church in Venice built around 421. It is most recognized for its 15th-century clock above the entrance of the church. It is also recognized for the red pillars and beautiful gold accents around the church itself.

listings.name: Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari
listings.content: The big friary church, fine example of Venetian Gothic architecture, with fine monuments and paintings of Titian, Belliniand Donatello, among which the famous 'Assunta' by Titian.

listings.name: Funerary monument of Claudio Monteverdi
listings.content: Tomb, composer (1567-1643) and champion of the early Baroque seconda pratica and then-new genre of opera.

listings.name: State Archive
listings.content: One of the largest archives in the world, in an old Franciscan monastery. Manuscripts, texts and documents related to the history of the Venetian Serenissima.

listings.name: Pizza 2000
listings.content: Pizza takeout

listings.name: Ostaria dai Zemei
listings.content: Down home cooking with Venezian style tapas

listings.name: Antico Forno
listings.content: A pizzeria

listings.name: Acqua e Mais
listings.content: Small plates

listings.name: Farini
listings.content: A bakery

listings.name: Ristorante Casa Cappellari
listings.content: Traditional Venetian cuisine with a warm atmosphere

listings.name: Antica Osteria Ruga Rialto
listings.content: Seafood specialties

listings.name: Farini
listings.content: A bistro

listings.name: Cantina Do Mori
listings.content: Venetian tapas

listings.name: Cantina Do Spade
listings.content: Venetian cuisine

listings.name: Antico Dolo
listings.content: An old seafood restaurant close to Rialto bridge: food comes from the adjacent Rialto Market daily. A complete dinner excluding wines could cost €35 each more or less.

listings.name: Trattoria Antiche Carampane
listings.content: In the heart of Venice, steps away from the Rialto Bridge, is this renowned restaurant where distinguished Venetian cuisine is served in a familiar setting.

listings.name: Gelateria Il Doge
listings.content: Excellent ice cream, all made on the premises (a rarity in Venice). Plenty of vegan options.

listings.name: La Bottiglia
listings.content: A small wine bar with excellent reviews. They offer a small but constantly changing selection of wines, complemented by excellent Italian street food and snacks.

listings.name: San Simeone Piccolo
listings.content: The last church built in Venice. One of the things that it is recognized for is the fact that they celebrate Tridentine Mass on Sundays. It is also recognized for its dome because it is used to make the church look taller than it is and the dome itself is entirely covered with lead sheet.

listings.name: San Giacomo dell'Orio Church
listings.content: Founded in the 9th century, the current church was built in 1225.

listings.name: Tolentini Church
listings.content: Historic church completed in 1714.

listings.name: Natural History Museum
listings.content: 11 exhibition halls with sections on palaeontology, explorations and nature. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Mocenigo Palace Museum
listings.content: A collection of clothes dating from the 18th century. Splendid interior. Collection of dresses and accessories, fabrics, books, figurines in various period costumes. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Ca' Pesaro - International Modern Art Gallery
listings.content: Modern art collection, paintings of the 19th and 20th century. A MUVE museum.
listings.price: Adults €14, reduced €11.50 (valid for both museums in the Ca' Pesaro)

listings.name: Ca' Pesaro - Museum of Oriental Art
listings.content: Beautiful palace housing the gallery of modern art focusing on Italian art in the 19th century as well as the Marco Polo Museum, a rich collection mainly of Asian exhibits (fabrics, clothes, armours, porcelain). A MUVE museum.
listings.price: Adults €14, reduced €11.50 (valid for both museums in the Ca' Pesaro)

listings.name: Giardini Papadopoli
listings.content: One of the few public parks in Venice.

listings.name: Bacaro Quebrado
listings.content: Cosy tavern

listings.name: Arcicchetti Bakaro
listings.content: A bistro

listings.name: Il Refolo
listings.content: Nice restaurant at a small piazza. Very good pizza as well as a decent menu.
listings.price: Pizza about €10, four-course meal with wine €60
listings.address: Ramo Quinto Gallion O del Pezzetto, 1459

listings.name: Osteria Ae Cravate
listings.content: This little restaurant is frequented by the professors of the nearby university. Warm welcome and a good eat. Try their raw artichoke salad or their fish of the day.

listings.name: Osteria Mocenigo
listings.content: Little restaurant frequented by locals. Be sure to try their antipasti. Excellent desserts too.

listings.name: Pasticceria Rio Marin
listings.content: Coffee shop that serves excellent tiramisùs.

listings.name: Gelateria Alaska
listings.content: Ice cream made with natural ingredients by Carlo Pistacchi, not only the owner but an artist, a poet and a philosopher.

listings.name: Osteria da Filo
listings.content: An excellent place to fill up on some aperitifs and meet the local student crowd. Aperol Spritz is €2.50, a bargain for being in central Venice. The bar also hosts live music from time to time.

listings.name: Bacareto da Lele
listings.content: A Venetian institution that's been around since 1968. This minuscule bar serves cheap wine, a small glass is just one euro, and excellent cichetti to go along. Queuing is the norm, but the bartenders are very quick and you'll be served in no time. A great place to rub shoulders with the real Venetians.

listings.name: Hotel Carlton on the Grand Canal
listings.content: Large hotel, just across the Grand Canal from the railway station.

listings.name: Hotel San Cassiano
listings.price: From €60 in January to €200+ in peak periods

listings.name: I Gesuati
listings.content: 18th-century Dominican church on the Giudecca canal. The classical style building has a well-lit interior and is exceptional in preserving its original layout and Rococo decoration intact. The church and almost all its sculpture and paintings were created within a 30-year period: construction began in 1725, the church was consecrated in 1743, and the last sculptural decoration was in place by 1755.

listings.name: S. Maria della Salute
listings.content: As a votive offering for the city's deliverance from the Black Plague, the church was designed in the then fashionable Baroque style. Construction began in 1631. Most of the objects of art housed in the church bear references to the Black Death. Because of its location between the Grand Canal and the Giudecca Canal, its dome was an important addition to the Venice skyline and soon became emblematic of the city, appearing in many artworks, such as those by Canaletto, Francesco Guardi, J. M. W. Turner, and John Singer Sargent.
listings.image: Santa Maria della Salute from Hotel Monaco.jpg

listings.name: Church of Saint Sebastian
listings.content: 16th-century Roman Catholic church, houses a cycle of paintings by the artist Paolo Veronese as well as paintings by Tintoretto and Titian. Includes the tomb of Paolo Veronese, a painter from Verona whose career was in Venice (1528-1588).

listings.name: Santa Maria del Carmelo church
listings.content: Large 14th-century Roman Catholic church.

listings.name: Punta della Dogana
listings.content: Former customs house, centre for contemporary art, permanent exhibition of works from the François Pinault Collection. Renovation by world renowned architect Tadao Ando.

listings.name: Ca' Rezzonico - Museum of 18th Century Venice
listings.content: Museum of the 18th century in Venice - attempts to revive the domestic atmosphere of Venetian nobilities. Furniture, interior decoration, paintings by Guardi, Canaletto, Tiepolo. On the third floor important paintings of the Venetian school. A MUVE museum.

listings.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
listings.content: Venice's most significant art museum which is also one of Italy's best. Among the most important paintings in the Accademia are: Gentile Bellini: Procession on St. Mark’s Square (1496) and Miracle of the Cross at the Bridge of S. Lorenzo (1500), Giovanni Bellini: Pieta (1500), Jacopo Bellini: Madonna with Child and Cherubs (ca. 1450), Paris Bordenone: A fisherman presents the ring of St. Mark to the doge (ca. 1535), Vittore Carpaccio: Legend of Saint Ursula (1490-1498), Cima da Conegliano: The Holy Virgin under the Orange Tree (ca. 1496), Giorgione (1477-1510): The Tempest and La Vecchia ("The Old Woman"), Andrea Mantegna (1431-1506): St. George, Veronese Paolo (1528-1588): The Feast in the House of Levi (1573), Tintoretto: The Miracles of St. Mark (1548), and Titian: Pietà (ca. 1576).

listings.name: Gallery Palazzo Cini
listings.content: Former residence of Italian industrialist Vittorio Cini who amassed large collection of Italian art. The gallery houses a collection of 15th and 16th cent paintings from Tuscany and Ferrara, period furniture, silver, ivory and ceramic objects.

listings.name: The Peggy Guggenheim Museum
listings.content: Offers a personal collection of modern art collected by Peggy Guggenheim. Peggy was an American married to modern artist Max Ernst, and funded a number of his contemporaries. The gallery includes a sculpture garden and works by Picasso, Kandinsky, Gorky, Tanguy, Duchamp, Pollock, Dali, and Mondrian.
listings.price: Adult €17, seniors (over 65 years) €15, students (25 years and under with valid student ID) €10, youth 10-18 €9, 9 and younger free

listings.name: Scuola Grande dei Carmini
listings.content: Painting cycles dedicated to the Madonna del Carmine, canvases by Tiepolo and Padoviano.

listings.name: Le Macchine di Leonardo a Venezia
listings.content: An exhibition in the Chiesa di San Barnaba showing around forty models of machines reproduced from Leonardo's codices. Some of the exhibits are interactive and copies of the codices are available for further reading. The church is an attraction in itself: it's the one under which Indiana Jones finds catacombs in The Last Crusade, by the way).

listings.name: Northern Giudecca canal walk
listings.content: It's a long and sunny walk along the Giudecca canal, protected during winter time from cold northerly winds for being exposed to south and shielded by buildings. You might find interesting to see how a gondola is made, stopping by the Squero (Venetian for small ship yard) across a canal near San Trovaso Church. It's one of the few still in business in town. With some luck, you'll see some gondole through various manufacturing steps (gondole are not straight to counterbalance the gondoliere push).

listings.name: Southern Giudecca canal walk
listings.content: Like the northern version you walk along the entire Giudecca canal, but in this case on the Giudecca island.

listings.name: Squero di San Trovaso
listings.content: Squero is Venetian for small ship yard.
listings.image: Venezia - Dorsoduro - Squero di San Trovaso.jpg

listings.name: The Avogaria Theatre
listings.content: The smallest theatre in Venice, housed in an unassuming former workshop.

listings.name: Pizza al volo
listings.content: Sells superb pizza by the (extremely large) slice in Campo Santa Margherita for approximately €1.80 a slice, €5 a whole pizza. It is by the fresh fish stall under a green awning.

listings.name: La Foca
listings.content: Pizza

listings.name: La Bitta
listings.content: This busy but friendly restaurant is in the more studenty area of Dorsoduro, and attracts a mixture of locals and tourists. They have some excellent Italian dishes, which are reflected in the prices, plus they have a great selection of wines.

listings.name: Osteria Ai Do Farai
listings.content: Serves fresh shell fish. Taste their spaghetti al dente with razor shells.

listings.name: Osteria Enoteca Ai Artisti
listings.content: An excellent restaurant, small but comfortable with a few tables alongside a tiny canal. Food is fresh and delicious, not too expensive. Large selection of wines. Menu changing daily.

listings.name: Chet Bar
listings.content: The closest thing to a dive bar you'll find in Venice, except that the cocktails actually are pretty good.

listings.name: Il Caffè Rosso
listings.content: Small but hugely popular café at Campo Santa Margherita. Serves coffee and sandwiches during the day, and excellent spritz during nights.

listings.name: Cantine del Vino gia Schiavi
listings.content: Inventive and delicious cicchetti; pile a plate with what you like, and the staff will pour you a glass of wine to match the selection. If it's too crowded inside, step out and find a space by the canal. A large and carefully curated selection of wines and spirits for purchase by the bottle. Joseph Brodsky, the American Nobel Prize winning poet and essayist, buried on San Michele, was a regular anytime he came to Venice.

listings.name: Ca' Della Corte
listings.content: A comfortable B&B in a quiet area. Warm and personal welcome. Breakfast (served in the room) could be improved (by going to pasticceria Tonolo and bringing your own cakes, e.g.).

listings.name: Ca' Zose
listings.content: A quiet street off S.M. Salute, by the S.M. Giglio traghetto (when it's operational, 50 cents will get you to S. Marco), within easy walk of either Accademia or the Zattere (no need to brave the hordes of tourists on the #1 line, take the #52 from bus or train station). The helpful staff speaks Italian, English, French and Veneto. 10% discount on rates if paid in cash - ask Walentina, the proprietress. All rooms are named after stars (in the sky, not of movie kind), and all have A/C (indispensable in summer). Buffet breakfast included.

listings.name: Locanda Gaffaro
listings.content: In a picturesque court near Piazzale Roma.

listings.name: Belmond Hotel Cipriani
listings.content: Opened in 1958 and long considered one of the leading luxury hotels of the world.

listings.name: Jewish Ghetto of Venice
listings.content: While racial and ethnic neighborhoods had existed prior to the Venetian Ghetto, Venice's ghetto was the first "ghetto" (coming from a Venetian word for the Iron Foundry that had been on the site) and "ghetto" eventually came to mean any neighborhood that was made up of a single ethnic/racial group. Today, Jewish life is still very active in the ghetto, and elsewhere in Venice, and is home to five synagogues. Visiting on Saturdays or late Fridays (the Jewish Sabbath) will prove very fruitless because all shops, restaurants, and other Jewish places will be closed.

listings.name: Jewish Museum
listings.content: Objects related to the social life of the Jewish community, in two synagogues of the 16th century.
listings.price: Entrance: adults €3, reduced €2. Entrance with guided tours to synagogues: adults €8.50, reduced €7

listings.name: Galleria Giorgio Franchetti Ca' d'Oro
listings.content: A collection of paintings and statues in a former palace from the 15th century. One of the best examples of Gothic architecture in Venice, sculptures, bronzes, paintings of Mantegna, Giorgione and Titian, Flemish and Dutch paintings.

listings.name: Oratorio dei Crociferi
listings.content: Small oratory facing the old monastery dei Crociferi, painting circle by Palma the Younger.

listings.name: Santa Maria di Nazareth Church
listings.content: Also known as Church of the Scalzi (Chiesa degli Scalzi), being the seat in the city of the Discalced Carmelites religious order (scalzi in Italian means "barefoot"). Built in the mid 17th century to the designs of Baldassarre Longhena and completed in the last decades of that century.

listings.name: Madonna dell'Orto Church
listings.content: With the grave and 10 paintings of Jacopo Robusti (Tintoretto) (1578-1594), and his tomb.

listings.name: I Gesuiti
listings.content: Also known as Church of Santa Maria Assunta, the current structure dates back to 1729.

listings.name: Scuola dell'Angelo Custode
listings.content: The only Lutheran church in Venice.

listings.name: S. Michele in Isola
listings.image: Chiesa di S.Michele in Isola, north exposure.jpg

listings.name: San Michele Cemetery
listings.content: Cemetery established following Napoleon Bonaparte's edict of 1804, part of the European circuit of monumental cemeteries. The Russian ballet director Sergei Diaghilev, the Austrian physicist Christan Doppler, the American poet Ezra Pound, the Russian composer Igor Stravinsky and the German-Italian composer Ermanno Wolf-Ferrari are buried in San Michele Cemetery.

listings.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli
listings.content: A perfect jewel box church, simple in form but ornamented with fine exterior marble facings.

listings.name: Teatro Malibran
listings.content: Teatro Malibran was built in 1678, and is now part of La Fenice. Tickets for opera, ballet, and symphony performances are available at La Fenice, various locations around the city, or by phone +39 041 2424.

listings.name: Venice Casino
listings.content: The oldest gambling house in the world, founded in 1638. The building dates back to the 15th century.
listings.price: Entrance €10, free if you are booked at selected hotels

listings.name: Orsoni Furnace
listings.content: One of the last industries left in Venice, the Orsoni Furnace produces fine glass panels and mosaics using the same technique since 1888. The small factory can only be visited on certain dates.

listings.name: Crepes House by PePe
listings.content: Savory and sweet crepes

listings.name: Al Timon
listings.content: Warm and local atmosphere in this little osteria where they serve great Italian vintages by the glass. If you're adventurous, try their tasty tripe. Good music inside, some table by the canal in the summer. Reservations on evenings is essential.

listings.name: La Colombina
listings.content: Artfully presented Venetian cuisine

listings.name: Trattoria Alla Fontana
listings.content: Warm canalside restaurant

listings.name: Ristorante Casa Bonita
listings.content: Generous portions of pasta and seafood

listings.name: Vino Vero
listings.content: Small wine bar with excellent selection, away from the tourist crowds. Outdoor seating next to one of the canals.

listings.name: Al Parlamento
listings.content: Another small bar, away from the main tourist arteries. Serves spritz, cocktails and beer with a view of the Cannaregio canal.

listings.name: Bed and Breakfast Ca'Dor
listings.content: Venetian style rooms in the centre, 3 minutes from Rialto's Bridge.
listings.price: Rooms about 55 in low-season, 100 in high season

listings.name: Alloggi Agli Artisti
listings.content: Guests can choose between rooms with bathroom en suite (with hairdryer), and rooms with sharing bathroom on the floor (cheaper).
listings.price: From €50 to €90 for a double room, depending on the season

listings.name: Antica Casa Carettoni Venice
listings.content: Close to Santa Lucia Train Station and the waterbus stops. 3 star hotel in an old convent offers accommodation starting at around €120-130 for a double room.

listings.name: Ca' Amadi
listings.content: In the old town centre, close to the famous Rialto Bridge. This 13th-century palace was once home to Marco Polo. Décor is keeping with the period, and the rooms are utterly charming. Original wall frescoes from the 1400s adorn the hotel.

listings.name: Continental Hotel Venice
listings.content: Three-star hotel in the Jewish Ghetto. A historic building belonged to a noble family, with 93 bedrooms (€95-194) capable to host any kind of guests.

listings.name: Ca' Gottardi
listings.content: Antico Palazzo Gottardi stands in Strada Nuova, between two buildings that look down onto the Canal Grande.

listings.name: Hotel Cà D'Oro
listings.content: The hotel is in a quiet corner of Cannaregio district, 5 minutes walk from the Rialto Bridge.

listings.name: Hotel il Mercante di Venezia
listings.content: Just off the Lista di Spagna by the Grand Canal, excellent access to the Station (Santa Lucia) and the waterbuses. Delicately appointed rooms from around €145.

listings.name: Hotel Nazionale Venice
listings.content: Three-star accommodation with 90 bedrooms divided in single, double, twin, triple and family, 100 metres away from the train station of Santa Lucia.
listings.price: €80 for a single and €160 for a family

listings.name: Palazzo Cendon - Il Piano Nobile
listings.content: Nice small hotel in good area with a few restaurants and bars.

listings.name: Hotel Giorgione
listings.content: In the centre, 10 minutes from Piazza San Marco, it was transformed into a hotel at the beginning of the 19th century and has been managed by the same family ever since.

listings.name: Bridge of Sighs
listings.content: Connecting the Doge's Palace with the prison. Persons convicted in the palace were passing to prison here, seeing the last of Venice before going into the dark prison area with no daylight. You can pass the bridge yourself during a visit to the Doge's Palace or view it from outside from the Ponte della Paglia.

listings.name: Napoleonic Gardens
listings.content: They are the largest green area in the historic center and are home to the Venice International Art Exhibition. The gardens contain lush vegetation, among which the various twentieth-century architectures of the pavilions are organised, mostly around a central avenue from which smaller paths branch off, characteristic for their shape and each one bearing the name of the nation hosted.

listings.name: San Giovanni e Paolo
listings.content: A fine, huge Dominican church with the tombs of many Doges. It shares its piazza with the fine Renaissance façade of the Scuola San Marco and an equestrian statue of the mercenary captain Bartolomeo Colleoni (see below).

listings.name: Santa Maria della Pietà
listings.content: A church that used to house an orphanage and hospital in the 18th century, it is known among classical music enthusiasts as the church where the Catholic priest and composer Antonio Vivaldi worked for most of his career.

listings.name: S. Francesco della Vigna
listings.address: Campo San Francesco della Vigna, Castello

listings.name: S. Giovanni in Bragora
listings.image: Chiesa di San Giovanni in Bragora - Venezia.jpg

listings.name: S. Maria Formosa
listings.content: The first church dedicated to "Mary of the Forms" was built on this spot in the VII century, when the Virgin ordered bishop Magnus to erect one, appearing to him as an exceedingly shapely woman. The current building, planned by Codussi, dates from the early XV century.
listings.image: Santa Maria Formosa Facciata e campanile.jpg

listings.name: Basilica di San Pietro di Castello
listings.content: Venice cathedral up to 1807, when the see was transferred to San Marco.

listings.name: Museo Diocesano
listings.content: Religious furniture and objects from now demolished churches and convents, one of the most appealing Romanesque cloisters of Venice.

listings.name: Museo Storico Navale
listings.content: Collection of relics from the Serenissima Republic of Venice, the Italian navy, and the ancient Arsenale shipyards, miniature models, uniforms and stadarts, collection of sea shells. The main building of the Naval Historical Museum (Riva S. Biasio) is closed for renovation works. It's possible to visit the Ships Pavilion in rio della Tana, Castello 2162 (close to the Naval Museum).

listings.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
listings.content: Residence-museum of the Querini-Stampa family, library, picture gallery, furniture and household objects from the 16th cent onwards, important paintings by Bellini, Palma, Ricci, Tiepolo and Longhi.

listings.name: Byzantine Pictures Museum (Greek Institute)
listings.content: Collection of Greek, Cretan and Venetian icons of the 14th to 18th century.

listings.name: Palazzo Grimani
listings.content: A jewel of Renaissance architecture that was opened as a Venetia civic museum in 2008, collections of paintings, archaeological collection of Greek and Roman artefacts, temporary exhibitions.

listings.name: Scuola Dalmatina di San Giorgio e Trifone
listings.content: Famous painting cycle by Vittore Carpaccio depicting the lives of St.George, Tryphon and Jerome.

listings.name: ASAC Library
listings.content: An annex at the Biennale gardens where the Biennale keeps records related to the Biennale exhibitions and to 20th century art, from 1895 onwards.

listings.name: Equestrian statue of Bartolomeo Colleoni
listings.content: The famous condottiere (1395–1475) had a long and remunerative career as captain of a mercenary army fighting for (or against, depending on the pay) the Republic, but died without an heir (8 daughters did not count) and bequeathed most of his significant wealth to Venice - on the condition that the grateful populace erect a monument to him in front of San Marco. The crafty council fulfilled the condition, with one detail - the statue stands in front of Scuola San Marco, the religious confraternity (now city hospital), not the Basilica. They didn't skimp on the sculptor, though, hiring Andrea del Verrocchio, teacher of Leonardo da Vinci. Look for the visual pun on the side of the postament - three inverted-comma-like shapes on the shield, the Colleoni coat of arms, are in fact three pairs of human testicles, or coglioni in Italian.

listings.name: Monuement for Gentile Bellini
listings.content: Venetian painter and official portraitist of the Doges (1439-1507), tomb.

listings.name: Monument for Giovanni Caboto
listings.content: Venetian explorer of North America who worked for the British (c. 1450-c. 1500).

listings.name: Giuseppe Verdi
listings.content: Composer of operas; Italian nationalist and national hero (1813-1901).

listings.name: Richard Wagner
listings.content: German opera composer (1813-1883).

listings.name: Chiesa della Pietà
listings.content: Between 1703 and 1740, Antonio Vivaldi taught the orchestra of the girls in the orphanage here, writing unparalleled music for them. Frequent concerts of his Four Seasons by a Baroque ensemble.

listings.name: Cip ciap
listings.content: Also sells delicious takeaway pizza by the slice (or slab) at similar prices. They also serve very tasty mini pizzas per kilogram.

listings.name: Osteria Alla Rampa
listings.content: A bistro

listings.name: Al Vecio Canton
listings.content: This small and atmospheric restaurant/pizzeria will absolutely enchant you. Famous for its traditional style pizza and seafood pasta, you will not only get it all at affordable prices (pizza from €7.50, pasta from €10, wine from €5/half litre), but you're also served by a most friendly and hearty staff. They top it off with a free home made digestivo (mostly vodka and lemon) at the end of your meal, just to make 100% sure you'll be coming back for more.

listings.name: Al Giardinetto
listings.content: Just behind the Piazza San Marco, this restaurant has a large private courtyard welcoming guests during good season. Seafood courses and Venetian specialities are served by Severino family.

listings.name: Pub Taverna L'Olandese Volante
listings.content: Located between the Rialto Bridge and Piazza San Marco. During the summertime there are tables outside when you can easily sit and rest after a day of wandering around this marvelous city. What is more, during the day pasta and other typical dishes are served at a budget price.

listings.name: Locanda Sant'Anna
listings.content: One star. Provides a family atmosphere with modern comforts. Quiet hotel with secure courtyard and some rooms with a canal view (for a higher price) overlooking the Isola di San Pietro. Common balcony over the canal. Includes typical Italian breakfast from 08:00-09:30 with coffee or hot chocolate and rolls, croissants, and toast. Easily accessible from the main bus/train station by vaporetto to stop 'S. Pietro' or 'Giardini'. Doors close at 01:00. Pay in cash for a discount.

listings.name: Ca' Bauta
listings.content: Housed in a 15th-century building, this quaint hotel has very spacious rooms with high ceilings and is adorned with stylish furniture and fittings. Has a friendly, multilingual staff who are always eager to assist you in planning tours, booking concert tickets, and making restaurant reservations. Rates from €70 per night.

listings.name: Ca' Valeri
listings.content: Residence where an atmosphere of charm and comfort defines an ambience of class.

listings.name: Hotel Ai Due Principi
listings.content: Boutique hotel.

listings.name: Hotel Canaletto Venice
listings.content: Along a scenic canal close to St. Mark’s Basilica. Decorated and furnished in the traditional Venetian manner, this hotel offers excellent service and rooms for two that start at around €110.

listings.name: Hotel Commercio e Pellegrino
listings.content: Comfortable hotel in the centre, easy to reach by public transport and 2 minutes on foot to Saint Mark’s Square.
listings.price: Single rooms from €80, doubles from €100 including taxes and breakfast

listings.name: Residenza Cà Bauta
listings.content: Few steps from Campo ss. Giovanni e Paolo, one of the most spectacular place of Venice. Double rooms are usually around €100-160 depending on season.

listings.name: Residenza Cá Malipiero Venice
listings.content: An historic building of the 16th century with a large selection of elegant single, double rooms and suites, capable to host up to four people and equipped with the best modern services expected by a three-star guest house.

listings.name: Hotel Tiepolo
listings.content: Small and elegant design hotel in the historic centre, a few steps away from Saint Mark's Square.

places.title: Burano
places.blurb: Burano is an island in the Venetian Lagoon, northern Italy, near Torcello at the northern end of the lagoon, known for its lace work and brightly coloured homes.

places.title: Biblioteca Marciana
places.blurb: The Marciana Library or Library of Saint Mark is a public library in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' d'Oro
places.blurb: The Ca' d'Oro, or Palazzo Santa Sofia, is a palace on the Grand Canal in Venice, northern Italy.

places.title: Ca' Rezzonico
places.blurb: Ca' Rezzonico (Italian pronunciation: [ˈkaretˈtsɔːniko]) is a palazzo and art museum on the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' Farsetti
places.blurb: Ca' Farsetti is a palace in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' da Mosto
places.blurb: The Ca' da Mosto is a 13th-century Venetian-Byzantine style palace, the oldest on the Grand Canal, located between the Rio dei Santi Apostoli and the Palazzo Bollani Erizzo, in the sestiere of Cannaregio in Venice, It…

places.title: Ca' Foscari
places.blurb: Ca' Foscari, the palace of the Foscari family, is a Gothic building on the waterfront of the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' Pesaro
places.blurb: Ca' Pesaro is a Baroque marble palace turned art museum, facing the Grand Canal of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Campo San Barnaba
places.blurb: Campo San Barnaba is a campo located in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Campo San Polo
places.blurb: The Campo San Polo is the largest campo in Venice, Italy, the second largest Venetian public square after the Piazza San Marco.

places.title: Campo Santa Margherita
places.blurb: Campo Santa Margherita is a city square in the sestiere of Dorsoduro of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' Sagredo
places.blurb: The Ca' Sagredo is a 14th-century Byzantine-Gothic style palace located on the corner of the Strada Nuova and Campo Santa Sofia, in the sestiere of Cannaregio in central Venice, Italy.

places.title: Angelo San Raffaele, Venice
places.blurb: The Chiesa dell'Angelo Raffaele is a church in Venice, northern Italy, located in the Dorsoduro sestiere.

places.title: Ca' Zenobio degli Armeni
places.blurb: The Ca' Zenobio degli Armeni is a three-story Baroque-style palace structure in the sestiere of Dorsoduro, in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ca' Tron
places.blurb: Ca' Tron is a palace in Venice, northern Italy, facing the Canal Grande.

places.title: Ateneo Veneto

places.title: Ca' Giustinian
places.blurb: The Ca' Giustinian, sometimes called the Palazzo Giustinian, is a palace on the Grand Canal in the San Marco sestiere of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Abbazia della Misericordia
places.blurb: The Church of the Abbey of Misericordia is a religious edifice in Venice, Italy, in the sestiere Cannaregio.

places.title: Caffè Lavena
places.blurb: Caffé Lavena is a café in the city of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Aperto '93
places.blurb: Aperto ’93 was a contemporary art exhibition conceived by Helena Kontova and Giancarlo Politi, and organized by Helena Kontova for the XLV edition of the Venice Biennale, directed by Achille Bonito Oliva in 1993.

places.title: Asplund Pavilion
places.blurb: The Asplund Pavilion is an Installation art structure built in 2018 in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Doge's Palace
places.blurb: The Doge's Palace is a palace built in Venetian Gothic style, and one of the main landmarks of the city of Venice in northern Italy.

places.title: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
places.blurb: The Peggy Guggenheim Collection is an art museum on the Grand Canal in the Dorsoduro sestiere of Venice, Italy.

places.title: St Mark's Basilica

places.title: Venetian Lagoon
places.blurb: The Venetian Lagoon, also Venice Lagoon or Lagoon of Venice, is an enclosed bay of the Adriatic Sea, in northern Italy, in which the city of Venice is situated.

places.title: Isola di San Michele
places.blurb: The Island of San Michele is an island in the Venetian Lagoon, Veneto, northern Italy.

places.title: Torcello
places.blurb: Torcello is a sparsely populated island at the northern end of the Venetian Lagoon, in north-eastern Italy.

places.title: Venice Lido
places.blurb: Venice Lido, commonly Lido or the Lido, is an 11-kilometre-long barrier island in the Venetian Lagoon, Northern Italy; it is home to about 20,400 residents.

places.title: Venice Biennale
places.blurb: The Venice Biennale is an international cultural exhibition hosted every two years in Venice, Italy.

places.title: La Fenice
places.blurb: Teatro La Fenice is a historic opera house in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Ospedale della Pietà
places.blurb: The Ospedale della Pietà was a convent, orphanage, and music school in Venice.

places.title: Il Redentore
places.blurb: The Chiesa del Santissimo Redentore, commonly known as Il Redentore, is a 16th-century Roman Catholic church located on Giudecca in the sestiere of Dorsoduro, in the city of Venice, Italy.

places.title: Rialto Bridge
places.blurb: The Rialto Bridge is the oldest of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.

places.title: St Mark's Campanile
places.blurb: St Mark's Campanile is the bell tower of St Mark's Basilica in Venice, Italy.

places.title: Venetian Ghetto
places.blurb: The Venetian Ghetto was the area of Venice in which Jews were forced to live by the government of the Venetian Republic.

places.title: Harry's Bar
places.blurb: Harry's Bar is a restaurant located at Calle Vallaresso 1323, Venice, Italy, owned by Cipriani S.A.

places.title: Gallerie dell'Accademia
places.blurb: The Gallerie dell'Accademia is a museum gallery of pre-19th-century art in Venice, northern Italy.

places.title: St Mark's Clocktower
places.blurb: The Clock Tower in Venice is an early Renaissance building on the north side of the Piazza San Marco, at the entrance to the Merceria.

places.title: Ponte delle Guglie
places.blurb: The Ponte delle Guglie is one of two bridges in Venice, Italy, to span the Cannaregio Canal.

places.title: Ponte dell'Accademia
places.blurb: The Ponte dell'Accademia is one of only four bridges to span the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.
